picks.what: View across the Loire, drawing with wash (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
picks.why: toned general view; cathedral towers and château clearly visible across the river

picks.what: The port seen from Les Salorges, engraving
picks.why: port of Nantes with ships and an early steamboat; caption cut; only 1080 px wide

picks.what: Town and harbor from a height, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: best general view: quays, sailing ships and the city skyline; frameless copy of #15

picks.what: Aerial photograph of the Loire and the city
picks.why: only real general view in P6; trim cuts the plane window frame; gray day, not a Quality image

gaps: P0: nothing. P1: nothing securely dated. P5: nothing.
notes: P2 alternative: #3 Merian/Zeiller panorama, Topographia Galliae 1656 (wide, black and white). Skipped #1/#2 Collignon after L. de Lincler (strong views, but Rijksmuseum dates only 1620–1687). Skipped #10 Nicolas Ozanne view of the port from Île Gloriette (Musée Dobrée, probably 1770s, but no date in the record). P6 is weak; #21 (Place de la Bourse street view, 2019) is the clean alternative.
